selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the story, what were the two soldiers told to do?
questions.answer: They were told to go to a faraway city.

questions.question: What message did the man at the fork give about the right road?
questions.answer: It was safe from loss and usually led to benefit and peace.

questions.question: Which road was said to bring loss to most travelers?
questions.answer: The road on the left.

questions.question: What two items did the right-road traveler carry?
questions.answer: A food bag and a rifle.

questions.question: What did the travelers on the right have to carry?
questions.answer: They had to carry a bag of food and a strong rifle.

questions.question: What seemed good about the left road at first?
questions.answer: It felt lighter and freer.

questions.question: What happened to the fortunate soldier’s heart and spirit after choosing that road?
questions.answer: He was saved from great fear and from needing people too much.

questions.question: Why was the obedient soldier not forced to do that?
questions.answer: He was prepared and followed the right path.

questions.question: How did the luckless soldier travel on the left road?
questions.answer: He kept asking people for help and was scared of many things.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who stayed faithful to his duty?
questions.answer: He reached the city safely and received honor.

questions.question: What two things does the passage compare?
questions.answer: It compares worship and sin by using a story.

questions.question: What were the soldiers doing when they came to the fork?
questions.answer: They were traveling together.

questions.question: What did the man say about most people who take the right road?
questions.answer: Most of them gain something good and feel peaceful.

questions.question: On which road did most people end up badly?
questions.answer: On the road to the left.

questions.question: Why did the right road require more effort from the soldiers?
questions.answer: They had to carry food and a weapon.

questions.question: What mistake did the second soldier make after hearing the warning?
questions.answer: He still chose the wrong road.

questions.question: Did that free choice bring real comfort to him in the end?
questions.answer: No. It brought fear, need, and trouble.

questions.question: How did the second soldier act toward people on the road?
questions.answer: He begged from them.

questions.question: What does the reward of the first soldier help us understand?
questions.answer: Faithful obedience brings honor and goodness.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who stayed obedient and kept his gear?
questions.answer: He reached the city peacefully and got a reward.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be found in worship?
questions.answer: Great good and happiness.

questions.question: How many soldiers are in the comparison story?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: How were the two soldiers alike at the beginning?
questions.answer: They both got the same order and started together.

questions.question: What did he say about the right road and peace of mind?
questions.answer: He said most people on it had calm hearts.
